scenes.heading: Error Handling
scenes.narration: Robust error handling decides how a pipeline reacts when something inevitably goes wrong, so failures stay contained.

scenes.heading: Ways failures are handled
bullets: Fail fast on unrecoverable, corrupting errors.
Route bad records to a dead-letter store.
Emit clear alerts with actionable context.
scenes.narration: Some errors, like a corrupt schema, should stop the pipeline immediately before damage spreads. Transient glitches, such as a brief network drop, deserve a retry instead. Records that simply cannot be processed go to a dead-letter store, and every failure raises an alert the team can act on.

scenes.heading: Transient vs permanent errors
scenes.narration: Transient errors are temporary and usually clear up on their own, so retrying with backoff resolves them. Permanent errors reflect genuinely broken data or logic, where retrying only wastes resources. Classifying the error correctly is the key to responding well.

scenes.heading: Isolating a bad record
scenes.narration: This handler distinguishes the two failure classes cleanly. Transient errors are re-raised so an outer retry mechanism can catch them. Validation errors, which retrying cannot fix, send the record to a dead-letter store with the reason logged, keeping the rest of the batch flowing.

scenes.text: Good error handling separates transient from permanent failures, retries the former, quarantines the latter, and always alerts with context.
scenes.narration: The goal is never to prevent every error, but to make sure each one is contained, visible, and easy to diagnose.
